info.desc: Smash is the third studio album by American punk rock band The Offspring, released on April 8, 1994 through Epitaph Records. The album was the band's last collaboration with record producer Thom Wilson, who produced their previous two albums, and also their last release on Epitaph (however, that label released their next album in Europe). Smash met high critical reception upon its release, and is now considered a classic punk rock album by fans, critics, and the band members themselves alike. podcast.body: Released on April 15, 1994, on the independent Epitaph label, this album initially received little fanfare, gaining its first audience among skateboarders and snowboarders. Its trajectory changed significantly when a fluke led an LA radio station to play its first single, an uncommon occurrence for Epitaph bands, and the song then spread to other stations. Epitaph invested $5,000 for a video, which MTV subsequently aired, causing an explosion in sales. An album initially expected to sell 60,000 copies over its lifetime suddenly sold that amount every couple of days, ultimately selling over 12 million copies and becoming the biggest selling independent record of all time. "the offspring had sold over 12 million copies of Smash, making it the biggest selling independent record of all time."

podcast.body: Released on April 8, 1994, *Smash* started slowly, initially gaining traction among skaters and snowboarders through songs featured in boarding videos. However, it soon took off when one of its songs received massive radio play in LA, leading to an MTV video. By August 1994, the album was selling thousands of copies every few hours, dwarfing previous sales figures (their *Ignition* album sold 60,000 total, while *Smash* sold that every three days). With estimated worldwide sales of around 20 million records, it became the second-highest-selling indie release in history for a decade and a half, trailing only Adele's *XL* Recordings release. The album produced four radio and video singles and, alongside Green Day's *Dookie*, played a crucial role in introducing millions to a new era of punk rock, displacing grunge as the top alt-rock sound by 1995. "When the Smash record was released on April 8th, 1994, it started slow. And the only people who noticed it were those skaters and snowboarders who heard an offspring song or two that had been picked up for a couple of boarding videos."

podcast.body: Released on April 8, 1994, coincidentally the same day Kurt Cobain was found dead, this was a fully independent album issued through Bad Religion's Epitaph label. Its timing was critical as grunge was waning and alt-rock audiences sought new sounds, with Cobain's death creating a creative vacuum that the album helped fill. Influenced by a revival in old school punk and Nirvana's melodic yet intense sound, "Smash" became part of the mid-90s "holy trinity of punk rock" alongside Green Day and Rancid. It is potentially the biggest-selling indie record of all time, achieving global sales of approximately 20 million copies. "Today it could be the biggest selling indie record of all time, with global sales somewhere around 20 million copies."

podcast.body: Released on April 8, 1994, the same day Kurt Cobain died, this third album from The Offspring had a recording budget of only $20,000 and was released on indie label Epitaph, leading to low initial expectations (aiming for 25,000 sales). However, it defied all predictions, reaching number 4 on Billboard by October and staying on the album charts for 101 weeks. It was the first album to go gold and platinum on Epitaph and became the biggest selling indie album of all time, with over 15 million copies sold worldwide. "It was the first album to go gold and platinum on Epitaph. It has since sold upwards of 15 million copies worldwide. This is the biggest selling indie album of all time."

podcast.body: Released on the Epitaph label on August 23, 1994, "Smash" by The Offspring is recognized as the biggest-selling indie rock record of all time. It has sold over 120,000 copies in Canada, more than 6 million in the US, and a staggering 18 million copies worldwide, figures that continue to grow. No other album released on an independent record label has come close to these sales figures. "Released on the epitaph label on August 23rd, 1994. It's the offspring and smash."

podcast.body: The Offspring released *Smash* just three days after the world learned of Kurt Cobain's death, on April 11, 1994. Recorded on a $20,000 budget in North Hollywood for Epitaph — the Orange County indie label co-founded by Bad Religion — it was expected to sell perhaps 15,000 copies if lucky. The timing was fortunate: Green Day's *Dookie* had already established that pop punk had an audience. *Smash* broke out via radio in Southern California and spread nationally and internationally, leaving Epitaph dazed as sales hit 500,000, then a million, two million, five million, ten million, and ultimately approximately 18 million worldwide — the biggest-selling independent rock record in history. "Would Green Day and the Offspring have become as big as they did had Nirvana continued?"

This album achieved explosive success, selling no fewer than 11 million copies worldwide, and became a major part of the mid-90s punk rock revival. "After two indie albums, they released a third indie record on April 8, 1994. It exploded, selling no fewer than 11 million copies around the world."
